resolved: Independent PostgreSQL, Redis and storage choices remove only the selected bundled service and retain the credentials appropriate to that mode.
Same-origin browser API routing and runtime server authentication remove the per-installation frontend build requirement.
The preset enables the upstream S3_DISABLE_ACL option so object ownership and private bucket policy govern uploads while reads use presigned URLs.
Only the HTTP proxy is public; application services run as non-root users with bounded compute.
Hosted managed sending, SMTP submission, payments, MCP and AI services are excluded.

Bundled MinIO has its own persistent volume and private administrative API. Backend uploads use its private endpoint; browser file reads use a separate public presign origin and retain bucket path and host.
Only an explicit bundled-storage flag allows creation of a missing bucket, with a bounded request and a mandatory authenticated access check. No ACL or bucket policy is changed.
Refresh-token authentication binds UUIDs as PostgreSQL parameters instead of raw SQL conditions.
runtime_notes: On 2026-10-04, all five native AMD64 runtime cases passed on an isolated cloud-VM development cluster using the public image digests in images.lock.json: all four bundled/external PostgreSQL and Redis combinations with bundled MinIO, plus all three dependencies external. Every case verified administrator/frontend sessions, private upload and signed download, token/account/object/Redis/PVC persistence after service restarts, and access rejection. Bundled MinIO created its missing private bucket. The external-dependency case also verified trusted PostgreSQL/Redis TLS, PostgreSQL verify-full plaintext refusal, and untrusted CA/hostname refusal. Evidence combines R4 first three passing cases with R5 last two; R4 overall failed only on probe cleanup, corrected by immutable UID deletion in R5. Both test clusters were removed. Exact run IDs, source manifests, timings and limits are recorded in README.md and the Hakopod runtime acceptance document. This is AMD64 development-fixture acceptance, not ARM64 runtime, public ACME/DNS, real email delivery, arbitrary providers, bucket CORS or backup restoration.
